summary.title: Best practices for writing SQL queries
summary.one_liner: You learn practical SQL habits for correctness, readability and performance, such as explicit JOINs, filtering early, avoiding functions on indexed columns, using CTEs, and reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE output.
keywords: leading wildcard like full table scan
takeaways: Get the query correct and readable first, and optimize only when the query is slow or runs often.
Eliminate rows early: filter in WHERE before aggregating, and use HAVING only for aggregate filters.
Avoid functions on indexed columns in WHERE and avoid leading % wildcards in LIKE so indexes can be used.
Use explicit JOIN ... ON with table aliases, prefer UNION ALL when duplicates are fine, and select named columns instead of *.
Use CTEs (WITH) to organize logic, and use EXPLAIN ANALYZE (PostgreSQL) to find bottlenecks and add indexes where they help.
summary.summary: This Metabase Learn article gives a brief guide to writing better SQL, aimed at data analysts and data scientists. It argues for prioritizing correctness and readability before performance, and walks through a typical query development workflow and the general order of query execution. Tips are grouped by clause (FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, UNION, ORDER BY), followed by sections on indexing, reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE output in PostgreSQL, and using Common Table Expressions. It includes short before-and-after code examples and briefly notes Metabase features such as the data reference tab, Snippets and the Query Builder.
